prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1310; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the claimant regarding a low-speed head-on collision at an intersection. Claimant reports the other vehicle crossed the center line during a turn. Claimant states she felt neck and lower back discomfort at the scene but declined transport by ambulance. Vehicle is drivable but has front-end damage. Photos requested and provided through the claimant's app upload.

Entry 2: Recorded the claimant's statement in full. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and says she prefers to handle the claim directly. Explained the coverage limits on the policy and the process for a rental vehicle. Claimant reports lower back strain and stiffness that worsened overnight. She has scheduled a visit with her primary care provider and will forward the visit notes when available.

Entry 3: Reviewed the police report submitted by the claimant. The responding officer noted both drivers were cooperative and no citations were issued. The other driver's insurer has been identified and a liability notice sent to them. Obtained a copy of the claimant's medical authorization form, which she signed and returned by mail.

Entry 4: Spoke with the claimant about the injury claim. She reports ongoing back pain rated as moderate and difficulty sitting for long periods. Provided her with a list of documents needed for the bodily injury portion of the claim, including itemized medical bills, prescriptions, and any time missed from work. Advised her she may want to keep a daily log of symptoms and activity limits.

Entry 5: Received the claimant's initial physician's note confirming a diagnosis of lumbar strain with a recommended course of physical therapy. Rental vehicle remains active. Vehicle repair estimate is under review and an appraiser has been assigned. Scheduled a follow-up call with the claimant in one week to check on treatment progress and outstanding documents.
